name: Lenskart Solutions Ltd

profile.what: Omnichannel eyewear company that designs, makes and sells prescription glasses, sunglasses, contact lenses and accessories. Owns the chain from frame and lens manufacturing (Bhiwadi, Rajasthan; Hyderabad plant under construction; 50% Thailand frame JV) and a central supply chain to 3,459 stores (Jun-2026: 2,725 India, 734 International), an app and website, home eye tests and remote optometry. Brands: Lenskart, John Jacobs, Vincent Chase, Owndays (Japan, acquired 2022), Meller (Spain, acquired FY26), Hustlr. International = Japan, Singapore and South-East Asia, the Middle East, Spain (Meller) and others (14 international markets, Q4FY26 letter).
profile.segmentsFy26: India ₹5,260 cr revenue (59%), International ₹3,606 cr (41%); segment EBITDA ₹1,070 cr (20.3%) and ₹691 cr (19.2%), AR FY26 note 41.
profile.scale: FY26: 23.8 mn eye tests, ~29 mn India eyewear units, 8.8 mn Lenskart Gold members, 20,000+ employees; ~50% of India revenue digitally influenced (55% in Q1FY27).
profile.src: AR FY26; Q4FY26 and Q1FY27 shareholders' letters

history.event: Incorporated in Delhi (CIN L33100DL2008PLC178355); 'digital first, then physical scale, then global platform' (AR FY26 timeline). Promoters: Peyush Bansal, Neha Bansal, Amit Chaudhary and Sumeet Kapahi (AR FY26).

Acquired a majority stake in Owndays, a Japan-headquartered eyewear chain (AR FY26 timeline): FY23 revenue jumped 152% to ₹3,788 cr and fixed assets to ₹5,067 cr (goodwill, Owndays stores; Screener). A further 4.40% was bought in FY25, with a ₹167 cr non-cash gain on the deferred consideration in FY25 other income (AR FY26 note 25).
Foundation stone for the Hyderabad eyewear plant (Telangana), ~₹1,500 cr estimated investment, production within two years (Construction World, 10-Mar-2025).

Consolidated master franchisee Dealskart and GeoIQ (location analytics), acquired Meller (Spain, sunglasses; ~US$35 mn brand at acquisition); acquisitions of subsidiaries ₹421 cr in the FY26 cash flow; 50% Thailand frame JV (Q3FY26).
Listed on NSE/BSE after a ₹7,278 cr IPO at ₹402 (band ₹382-402): fresh issue 5.35 cr shares (₹2,150 cr) and offer for sale 12.76 cr shares (₹5,128 cr). First close ₹403.1.
603 net new stores (542 India, 254 of them in Tier 2+; 61 International) to 3,327; B by Lenskart AI smart glasses launched in Q4FY26.

guidance.text: Track annual volume growth of ~25% as 'the cleanest yardstick'; do not use any single quarter as the base expectation (FY26 volume +24.7%, Q1FY27 +25.7%)
Net new store additions in FY27 'at or around FY26 levels' (603 in FY26); 132 added in Q1FY27. India 'points past 10,000 stores' over time (6,100 unserved pin codes, ~3,000 densification)

guidance.text: Long-term steady-state EBITDA (pre-IndAS 116) margin ~25% (FY26 ~11%, Q1FY27 13.3%); near-term margins may vary with store phasing, marketing and long-term bets
guidance.src: Q4FY26 letter; reiterated in the Q1FY27 letter

guidance.text: Hyderabad plant (~50 mn pairs a year) commissioning in ~18 months from May-2026, with a large part of the initial outlay in FY27; Q1FY27 capex ₹207 cr (stores ₹75 cr, plant ₹132 cr), funded from operating cash
Measured store additions (16 in Q1FY27); margins to be judged on a trailing-twelve-month basis; Q1 benefits from the sunglasses season

accounting: Two bases: reported (statutory) and proforma (Dealskart, GeoIQ, Meller consolidated in prior periods); the letters quote proforma growth, so Q1FY27 revenue growth is 33.6% proforma vs 43.3% reported.

EBITDA is after Ind AS 116 (rent excluded; right-of-use depreciation ₹704 cr and lease interest ₹163 cr in FY26). Lease principal paid ₹620 cr in FY26 sits in financing cash flow; we treat it as a cost of running stores.
FY25 profit includes a ₹167 cr non-cash gain on the Owndays deferred consideration (FY25 adjusted PAT ₹130 cr; the company's ₹2,140 Mn H1 and ₹5,300 Mn FY26 'adjusted PAT' are proforma).
Minority interests: ₹7.3 cr of FY26 profit (owners ₹493.6 cr of ₹501.0 cr); Screener's Net Profit is before minorities, so LENSKART.patch.js uses 'Profit for EPS'.
FY26 exceptional loss ₹15.7 cr (investment impairment ₹10.4 cr, IPO expenses ₹5.3 cr); FY26 other income includes ₹15.2 cr of liabilities written back and a ₹4.0 cr call-option fair-value gain.
